decisions.justification: The agent asked whether to abort, skip colliding files, or choose alternative names, and the user selected abort.
The first option explicitly proposed aborting before renaming anything, versus the partial-application skip option, and the user selected it.
Neither party decided whether files already matching the target naming scheme belong in the rename set.
The session never distinguished an unrelated occupied target from one occupied by a source that would be renamed later in the same run.
The user added unprompted: "make sure running the same command twice does nothing the second time."
The user added unprompted: "treat names that differ only by upper/lower case as a clash on this machine."
The agent's design approval question proposed listing every collision on stderr and exiting nonzero, and the user answered yes.
The session never discussed whether preview or confirmation should be included or relied upon.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr
mustAchieveMet: no existing file is ever overwritten

notes: The session clearly chose a collision policy and implemented aggregate preflight reporting, case-insensitive checks, and second-run no-ops. It missed self-inclusion and transient-collision semantics, and the implementation is not fully atomic because non-collision failures during the rename loop can still leave earlier renames applied.
